question: Why might a chatbot state a made-up fact with full confidence?

options.text: It secretly prefers lying to users
It predicts plausible-sounding words, not verified truth
It ran out of memory mid-sentence

teachLine: The model picks words that fit the pattern of a good answer, and a smooth-sounding wrong answer can fit that pattern too. Confidence in tone isn't the same as being right.
callbackFact: LLMs can produce fluent, confident-sounding statements that are factually false ('hallucinations') because they optimize for plausible next tokens, not verified accuracy.
